newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS PRESS - MAY 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BRITISH BUSINESS PRESS - MAY 15.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by
The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- MINISTER LASHES INSURANCE CHIEFS

Insurance chiefs have received 'an unprecedented tongue- lashing' from Helen Liddell, economic secretary to the Treasury, over delays in sorting out the 4 billion stg personal pensions scandal. Liddell told 28 chief executives and directors of insurance companies that their 'reprehensible behaviour had damaged the reputations of the firms concerned and the whole financial services sector'.
-- WARBURG SET TO BID FOR DILLON READ

SBC Warburg WSG.L is reported to be considering a bid of more than $500 million for US investment bank Dillon Read. The news follows an announcement from Dutch group ING that it had withdrawn from acquisition talks with Dillon Read. ING is expected to benefit by about $100 million from any deal as it negotiated a 'tag along' clause during its talks with Dillon.
-- BA HOPES BIG NEW RIVAL WILL SMOOTH WAY FOR ITS ALLIANCE

The announcement of plans for a rival airline alliance has spurred British Airways and American Airlines to increase the pressure on regulatory authorities to approve their tie-up. BA and AA reacted following news of the creation of Star Alliance, a strengthening of ties between United Airlines, Lufthansa, Scandinavian Air Systems, Air Canada and Thai Airways.
THE TIMES
-- HORLICK IN LINE FOR 1 MILLION STG JOB

Former Morgan Grenfell fund manager Nicola Horlick is in line for a 1 million stg salary when she joins the London office of Societe Generale, France's largest fund manager. The move will see Horlick link up again with John Richards, currently head of investment for UK institutions at Mercury Asset Management (MAM). Horlick and Richards began their City careers at MAM 14 years ago.
-- MERRYDOWN TURNS TWO DOGS LOOSE

Cider company Merrydown has passed the distribution rights for Two Dogs, its alcopop brand, to Scottish & Newcastle . The move follows a downturn in sales in the final quarter, with Merrydown conceding it had been unable to maintain distribution and provide sufficient advertising back-up in the competitive alcopops market.
-- INVESTMENT BOOSTS CU PROFITS

Insurer Commercial Union has reported first quarter pre-tax profits of 102 million stg. Life assurance operating profits were 62 million stg, compared to 58 million stg for the same period the previous year. The figures were in the middle of expectations. General insurance operating profits were 67 million stg, up from 64 million stg.
THE GUARDIAN
-- REVOLT FORCES SHELL TO BUCKLE

In an eventful annual meeting at Shell, the oil group won a vote on corporate responsibility while losing the argument. The motion, which urged Shell to adopt higher environmental and social standards, had been backed by church and human rights groups and the pension fund adviser Pirc. It was defeated by a vote of roughly eight to one, largely due to the block votes of major financial institutions.
-- SAFEWAY TO MAKE 8,000 NEW JOBS

Supermarkets group Safeway has said it plans to create 8,000 new jobs over the next two years. Details of the expansion plans were given as the group confounded City pessimists by unveiling stronger than expected sales and profit figures. Safeway had warned in February that its full-year profits were in danger of falling below expectations because of slowing sales and falling food prices.
-- US AIRCRAFT FIRM ACCUSES BRUSSELS OF AIRBUS BIAS

McDonnell Douglas, the US aircraft manufacturer, has criticised European Union competition commissioner Karel van Miert for threatening to block the proposed merger between MDD and Boeing. MDD chairman Harry Stonecipher launched a stinging personal attack on van Miert, accusing him of partisan advocacy for the European consortium Airbus Industrie.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- SUGEN TAKES SECOND SHOT AT UK FLOATATION

California-based biotechnology company Sugen, which is 20 percent owned by Britain's Zeneca, is planning a UK stock market float this summer which will value the company at around $150 million (92 million stg). The move follows the recent revival of confidence in shares in the biotechnology sector in the UK, as Sugen was forced to defer floatation plans last year when prices began to slump.
-- HOME-OWNERS 'PAY TOO MUCH'

Figures issued by Yorkshire Bank claim that millions of mortgage borrowers will pay 73 billion stg more in interest payments than they should over the next 25 years because lenders charge them for repayments they have already made. The bank said that for an average 51,000 stg repayment loan on which interest is charged each year, a home-owner would overpay more than 13,500 stg in interest costs over 25 years.
-- SCOTTISH RADIO PLANS FURTHER EXPANSION

Scottish Radio Holdings has indicated that it may bid for Scot FM as it steps up its attempts to obtain a second FM radio licence. The rapidly-expanding group has said it may also apply for next-year's central Scotland licence. The comments came as Scottish reported a 39 per cent surge in interim pre-tax profits, to 4.5 million stg.
